title: BlindToChange: AI Agents Can Find Changes When Asked But Do They Look When Needed?
abstract: arXiv:2610.41435v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Given that AI agents can search the web broadly and deeply in real time, it is tempting to conclude that their outputs account for recent world events. We show that this conclusion does not hold in practice. While agents can search and easily find recent changes, the correctness of their responses depends on whether they search and what they search for. Popular agentic search benchmarks like BrowseComp cannot expose failures wherein agents do not recognize their own assumptions that should be verified, since these benchmarks explicitly state what needs to be found. In contrast, many user requests state only the final information need (e.g., an itinerary for a trip), leaving the agent to discover relevant changes (e.g., the temporary closure of a museum) and account for their consequences. translated_title: BlindToChange：AI智能体在被告知时能找到变化，但它们在需要时会主动去查看吗？
translated_abstract: 鉴于AI智能体能够实时对网络进行广泛而深入的搜索，人们很容易认为其输出结果已经考虑了最新的世界动态。我们表明这一结论在实践中并不成立。虽然智能体可以搜索并轻松找到近期变化，但其回答的正确性取决于它们是否进行了搜索以及搜索了什么。像BrowseComp这样的流行智能体搜索基准无法暴露智能体未能意识到自身假设需要验证的失败情况，因为这些基准明确指出了需要查找的内容。相比之下，许多用户请求仅陈述最终的信息需求（例如一次旅行的行程安排），而需要智能体自行发现相关的变化（例如某博物馆临时闭馆）并考虑其影响。为了凸显这类缺陷，我们提出了BlindToChange，一个衡量智能体能否主动发现影响其回答的近期事件的基准。
tldr: 提出BlindToChange基准，揭示AI智能体虽能在明确要求下找到近期变化，但在用户仅陈述信息需求时往往不会主动发现并考虑影响回答的最新事件。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces BlindToChange, a benchmark revealing that AI agents can find recent changes when explicitly asked, but fail to proactively discover and account for recent events affecting their responses when users only state their final information needs.
